parameters.name: city
parameters.description: Invented place names, so that no model can answer from world knowledge.

parameters.name: distractor_cities
parameters.description: Rows that surround the planted row in the document.

derivations.name: other_cities
derivations.expr: [name for name in distractor_cities if name != city]
derivations.description: Distractor rows never collide with the planted row.

derivations.name: rows
derivations.expr: join("\n", [f"  {other_cities[i]:<14} {distractor_units[i]:>6} units    {distractor_units[i] % 40:>3} returned" for i in range(len(other_cities))])

derivations.name: answer
derivations.expr: {"city": city, "quarter": quarter, "year": year, "units": units, "returns": returns, "net_units": net_units}

notes: json_schema runs before exact on purpose: a wrong extraction should report a schema violation, which names the offending field, rather than a string mismatch, which does not. The place names are invented so the ground truth cannot leak in from pretraining.
